notes: cellular_test.py and ota.check() both passed cleanly on the manifest (pure ASCII JSON), but ota.update() corrupted config.py: 'HTTPREAD reassembled 1024 bytes but AT+HTTPACTION declared 1450'. Real root cause: config.py's header comment contains an em dash (3 UTF-8 bytes, 1 character after decoding) landing inside the first 1024-byte chunk. parse_http_read() was slicing an already-DECODED STRING by the modem's declared BYTE lengths -- fine for pure-ASCII payloads like the manifest, but every multi-byte character before a chunk boundary shrinks the string 1-2 characters short of its declared byte count, throwing off every later offset and causing the next chunk's marker search to miss entirely. Fixed: parse_http_read() and read_http_data() now operate on raw bytes throughout, decoding to UTF-8 only once at the very end after all chunks are correctly reassembled by exact byte length. Verified against the actual real config.py file (byte-for-byte identical reassembly) plus a dedicated synthetic UTF-8-straddling-a-boundary test, both via the mock-UART pipeline with fragmented delivery.
